Spontaneous Communications: The public is encouraged to address the Parks & Recreation Commission on any matter listed on the
agenda or on any other matter within its jurisdiction. The Parks & Recreation Commission will hear public comments on items listed
on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote. The Parks & Recreation Commission will hear public comments
on matters not listed on the agenda during the Spontaneous Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain
emergency or special circumstances exist.  The Parks & Recreation Commission may request from staff to investigate and/or
schedule certain matters for consideration at a future Commission or City Council meeting.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a Commission meeting
or other services offered by this City, please contact City Hall at (626) 430-2200. Assisted listening devices are available at this
meeting. Ask the Deputy City Clerk if you desire to use thi s device. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet
can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with disabilities. Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the
meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide
accessibility to the meeting or service.

Note: Staff reports are available for inspection at the office of the Deputy City Clerk, City Hall, 5050 N. Irwindale Avenue, during
regular business hours (8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday through Thursday).

  Code of Ethics

As City of Irwind ale Parks & Recreation Commissioners, our fund amental duty is to serve the public good. We are
committed to the principle of an efficient and professional loca l govern ment. We wil l be exemplary in obeying the letter
and spirit of Loca l, State and Federal laws and City policies affecting the operat ion of t he government and in our private
life. We w ill be independent and impartial in our judgment and actions.

We will work for t he commo n good of the City of Irwindale community and not for any private or persona l interest. We
will endeavor to treat all people with respect and civility. We will commit to observe the highest standards of morality
and integrity, and to faithfully discharge the duties of ou r office regardless of personal consideration. We shall refrain
from abusive conduct, persona l charges or verbal attacks upon the character or motives of others.

We w ill inform ourselves on public issues, listen attentive ly to public discussions before t he body, and focus on t he
business at hand. We will base our decisions on the merit and substance of that business. We will be fair and equitable
in all actions, claims or transactions. We sha ll not use our official position to influence government decisions in which
we have a financial interest or where we have a personal relationship that could present a conflict of interest, or create
a perception of a conflict of interest.

We shall not take adva ntage of services or opportunities for personal ga in by virtue of our public office that are not
ava ilable to the public in general. We sha ll refra in from accepting gifts, favors or promises of f uture benefit that might
comprom ise our independence of j udgment or action or give the appearance of being compromised.

We will behave in a manner that does not bring discred it or embarrassment to the City of Irwindale. We will be honest
in thought and deed in both our personal and official lives.

Ultimate responsibility fo r complying with t his Code of Ethics re sts w ith the individua l elected official. In addition to any
other penalty as provided by law, violation of th is Code of Ethi cs may be used as a basis for disciplina ry action or ce nsure
of a Commissioner.

These things we hereby pledge to do in the interest and purposes for which our govern ment has been established.

  SPONTANEOUS COMMUNICATIONS
This is the time set aside for members of the audience to speak on items not on this agenda. State law prohibits any Commission
discussion or action on such communications unless 1) the Commission by majority vote finds that a catastrophe or emergency
exists; or 2) the Commission by at least four votes finds that the matter (and need for action thereon) arose within the last five days.
Since the Commission cannot (except as stated) participate it is requested that all such communications be made in writing so as to
be included on the next agenda for full discussion and action. If a member of the audience feels he or she must proceed tonight,
then each speaker will be limited to 2 minutes and each subject limited to 6 minutes, unless such time limits are extended.

 IRWINDALE CITY COUNCIL CHAMBERS  APRIL 3, 2019
5050 N. IRWINDALE AVENUE  WEDNESDAY
IRWINDALE, CALIFORNIA 91706  6:00 P.M.

The Irwindale PARKS & RECREATION COMMISSION met in regular session at the above time
and place.

ROLL CALL:  Present: Commissioners Jason Hickman, Marguerite S. Lopez,
  Belen Zepeda; Vice Chair Paula Fraijo; Chair Dan Diaz

  Also present: William Tam, City Manager; Eva Carreon, Director of
  Finance; Priscilla Zepeda, Recreation Manager, Elizabeth
  Rodriguez, Public Works Services Manager; Pedro Rodriguez Jr. ,
  Public Works Maintenance Supervisor; and Armando Hegdahl,
  Management Analyst

SPONTANEOUS
COMMUNICATIONS  There were no speakers.

CONSENT CALENDAR

MOTION  A motion was made by Vice Chair Fraijo, seconded by
  Commissioner Lopez, to approve the Consent Calendar. The motion
  was unanimously approved.

ITEM NO. 1A  MINUTES
MINUTES
  The following minutes were approved as presented:

  1) Regular meeting held March 6, 2019.

NEW BUSINESS

ITEM NO. 2A  USER FEES FOR RECREATION DEPARTMENT
USER FEES FOR
RECREATION DEPT.

MANAGER ZEPEDA  Manager Zepeda provided the verbal report. She advised that the
  fees being charged by the Recreation Department have not changed
  since 2004, and elaborated on each of the proposed fee changes for
  the various Recreation facilities and programs. She further explained
  the need for consistent fees across all city departments, the
  approved uses of city facilities, insurance requirements, and the
  amount of staff time expended in setting up facilities for functions by
  outside parties.

CITY MANAGER TAM  City Manager Tam explained the requirement by the city's insurance
  pool to require insurance for city facilities when rented out for various
  functions.
 PARKS & RECREATION COMMISSION MINUTES  APRIL 3, 2019
REGULAR MEETING  PAGE2

DISCUSSION HELD  Lengthy discussion was held relating to the amount of use of
  Recreation facilities and programs by Irwindale residents vs. non-
  residents, as well as the proposed pricing tiers. The commission
  advocated for decreasing costs to residents.

DENA ZEPEDA  Dena Zepeda spoke about the rental and use/availability of facilities ,
  and suggested increasing costs to non-residents and decreasing
  costs to residents.

CARMEN ROMAN  Carmen Roman suggested increasing costs to non-residents and
  providing free programs, trips, and activities to residents, with even
  lower costs to resident seniors, and spoke on the cleanliness of the
  exercise machines at the gym.

MANAGER ZEPEDA  Manager Zepeda noted the changes requested by the Commission
  and advised that they will be presented to the City Council for final
  determination .

RECREATION
DEPARTMENT UPDATE
RECREATION  Recreation Manager Zepeda provided the following update:
MANAGER ZEPEDA
  1) The following trips were held:
  A) Teeny Tots - Magical Playground - March 20
  B) Tiny Tots - Aquarium of the Pacific - March 21
  C) Family Trip - Carlsbad Flower Fields - March 30
  D) Day Camp - AMC Covina - April 2
  2) The following trips have been scheduled for April:
  A) Teen Trip - Disneyland - April 3
  B) Day Camp - Disneyland - April 4
  C) Dodgers vs. Pirates - April 27
  3) Registrations are being accepted for Spring Aquafitness and Lap
  Swimming
  4) The Irwindale Cheer Program participants placed 1st at their
  competition held March 30. They will also compete on April 5th at
  Sierra Vista High School.
  5) She recognized Recreation Supervisor Marez for her efforts in
  organizing the Movies in the Park and Music in the Park events.
  6) She also thanked the Public Works Department for installing a
  Bottle Filling Station at the Recreation Center.
  7) She then thanked the IT Department, which assisted the
  Recreation Department in securing Push-to-Talk telephones.
  8) Both she and Recreation Supervisor Marez attended the 2019
  CPRS Conference.
  9) Finally, she introduced the two new city mascots: Pebbles and
  Rocky.
 PARKS & RECREATION COMMISSION MINUTES  APRIL 3, 2019
REGULAR MEETING  PAGE3

PUBLIC WORKS
DEPARTMENT UPDATE

PUBLIC WORKS MAINT. Public Works Maintenance Supervisor Rodriguez provided the
SUPERVISOR  following report:
RODRIGUEZ
  1) An electrician has completed the repairs of the lighting at El Nido
  Park.
  2) The concrete panels near the stairway at the rear of the gym
  have been repaired , though other panels are in need of repair.
  3) The air conditioning unit at the gym lobby has been repaired.
  4) The guard rail at the Skate Park has been painted with primer
  and is being prepared to be painted turquoise.
  5) He also thanked the Commission for adjourning the March
  meeting in memory of Blas "Sonny" Gonzales.

DENA ZEPEDA  Dena Zepeda requested that the barbecue grills be cleaned, to which
  Supervisor Rodriguez advised that the dirty conditions of the grills is
  due to frequent vandalism . Staff cleans the grills almost daily.

MANAGER RODRIGUEZ Manager Rodriguez added that some of the bbq pits will be replaced.

ASSISTANT CITY
MANAGER UPDATE

ITEM NO. 5A  IRWINDALE PARK IMPROVEMENT PROJECT PHASES 2 AND 3 -
IRWINDALE PARK  VERBAL UPDATE
IMPROVEMENT
PROJECT PHASES 2
AND 3 - VERBAL
UPDATE

CITY MANAGER TAM  City Manager Tam presented his report, which outlined the
  commission's prior suggestions on how to improve Irwindale Park, to
  be completed in three phases. Most phases were previously put on
  hold until funding could be identified , which has now occurred. He
  displayed a map with the commission 's previous suggestions, which
  included a bus drop-off location and memorial garden, among other
  items. He added that the same architect that designed the project
  originally will be retained for these next phases. Finally, a workshop
  with the final design will held for input by the City Council , hopefully
  within 90 days.

CARMEN ROMAN  Carmen Roman suggested recognizing the women who have made
  significant contributions to the city, to which City Manager Tam
  advised that staff has worked on a Dedication Policy that will
  hopefully be completed and incorporated into this project.
 PARKS & RECREATION COMMISSION MINUTES  APRIL 3, 2019
REGULAR MEETING  PAGE4

COMMISSIONER ITEMS

COMMISSIONER  Responding to a question by Commissioner Zepeda, Manager
ZEPEDA  Zepeda indicated that the Recreation Department has advertised on
  social media, flyers, and will even hang a banner to notify the public
  that the Movies in the Park activities will be held at Jardin de Roca
  Park. She noted that the change was made since the noise
  emanating from the pool while in use interferes with the audio from
  the movies when they were held at Irwindale Park.

DENA ZEPEDA  Dena Zepeda expressed concern over homeless individuals during
  the Movies in the Park activities if they were held at Jardin de Roca
  Park.

CARMEN ROMAN  Carmen Roman requested that the park be cleaned.

VICE CHAIR FRAIJO  Responding to Vice Chair Fraijo's question, Manager Rodriguez
  advised that staff will work with Trammell Crow to ensure that the
  fencing around the park is repaired in time for the movies. She
  added that she would also collaborate with the Police Department to
  ensure a safe environment. Vice Chair Fraijo suggested discussing
  how successful the program turns out at its September meeting. She
  also thanked both the Public Works and Recreation Departments for
  their wonderful work.

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Lopez thanked staff for working on the updated Fee
LOPEZ  Schedule and expressed her optimism over the ongoing Park
  Improvement Project.

VICE CHAIR FRAIJO  Vice Chair Fraijo requested that the Commission hold a walk-through
  of Irwindale Park during the May commission meeting and that a
  member of the Police Department update the commission regarding
  the Summer Park Patrol plans at the June meeting. She also
  thanked Recreation and Public Works staff for their hard work in
  addressing all of the commission's concerns.

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Hickman echoed Vice Chair Fraijo's comments and
HICKMAN  thanked staff for their dedication.

ADJOURNMENT  There being no further business to conduct, the meeting was
  adjourned at 7:24 p.m., in memory of Richard Breceda.

  Armando Hegdahl, CMC
  Management Analyst

  AGENDA REPORT
  Parks and Recreation Commission

 Date:  May 1, 2019
 To:  Honorable Chair and Members of the Parks and Recreation Commission
 From:  Priscilla Zepeda, Recreation Manager
 Issue:  Recommendation for Playground Plaques at all City Playgrounds

Staff Recommendation:

That the Parks and Recreation Commission provide input and a formal recommendation
for the proposed playground plaques for the playgrounds located in Irwindale Park, Jardin
de Roca Park, El Nido Park and Little Park of Irwindale.

Background and Analysis:

At the request of City Council, staff has been directed to design and install dedication
plaques for each of the four playgrounds that were remodeled in 2018. These plaques
will be located adjacent to the playgrounds at Irwindale Park, Jardin de Roca Park, El
Nido Park and Little Park of Irwindale. Staff is seeking a formal recommendation
regarding the design of these plaques.

Staff is bringing for your consideration and approval a design consistent with designs
previously made for dedication plaques for other city projects. The design is similar to
the mock ups that were on display at the ribbon cutting ceremonies for each of the parks.
There is one exception, the removal of the Youth First logo. The logo was omitted due to
the difficulty replicating the intricate details within the logo. Attached are the designs for
your review.

Prepared By/Contact:  Priscilla Zepeda, Recreation Manager
